review_finding.finding: A multi-ref Git transaction can leave the managed branch visible while the publication receipt is absent; the former create/reject_if_exists replay guard then rejected the service's own partial publication as BRANCH_ALREADY_EXISTS.

operator_supplied_evidence.scope: standalone isolated bare-repository Git mechanism test

fix.subject: fix: recover partial managed branch publication
protocol: Derive publication identity from mirror key, case-folded branch, and assignment ID; reject mismatched publication/lease identity.
Commit a canonical immutable Git-blob intent ref before mutating the branch.
Bind the intent to repository, mirror, branch, assignment, publication ID, source/selected commits, frozen policy, expected head, and observed local/remote predecessors.
CAS-publish the branch, then CAS-create the completion receipt as separate ref operations.
Allow branch-only recovery only when the exact durable intent matches; same-SHA without intent remains BRANCH_ALREADY_EXISTS.
Reclaim only an exact intent-bound lock with the exact expected object ID while holding the service-owned mirror mutation lock.
Retain compatibility with successful legacy receipts that predate intent records.
Leave ambiguous legacy branch-only states fail-closed for explicit operator recovery.
fix.ownership_boundary: The managed bare mirror is documented as service-owned and single-writer; unmanaged Git mutation is unsupported.

limitations: No fresh disposable managed E2E flow was started because the operator constraints prohibit a new sprint and start-from-git; historical IE2E evidence remains lineage evidence, not exact-fixed-head runtime proof.
The actual-provider fault test covers Alpine Linux, Git files refs, and receipt-rename EIO/process-exit faults; it is not a Windows crash matrix and does not claim host power-loss durability.
The stale-lock protocol relies on the documented service-owned single-writer mirror boundary.
A legacy branch-only partial publication without an intent remains intentionally fail-closed and requires explicit operator recovery.
The generic staging diagnostic remains 16/18 with two disclosed filesystem-alias errors.
Protected PR approvals and repository checks are not supplied by local qualification.
